verses.text: That day Jesus left the house and sat by the sea.
Huge crowds gathered around him, so he got into a boat and sat down. Everyone else stood on the shore.
He taught them many things through parables. “A farmer went out to scatter seed,
and some seed fell along the path. Birds came and ate it.
Some fell on shallow, rocky ground with little soil. It sprang up quickly because the soil wasn’t deep,
but when the sun came up, the plants were scorched. They withered because they had no roots.
Some seed fell among thornbushes, which grew up and choked the plants.
Other seed fell on good soil and produced a crop—some a hundred times what was sown, some sixty, and some thirty.
Anyone with ears should listen.”
The disciples came and asked him, “Why do you teach the crowds through parables?”
He answered, “You’ve been given the ability to understand the secrets of the Kingdom of Heaven, but they haven’t.
Whoever has will be given more and will have plenty. Whoever doesn’t have will lose even what they have.
That’s why I speak to them in parables: they look but don’t really see; they listen but don’t really hear or understand.
Isaiah’s prophecy is coming true in them: ‘You’ll hear, but you won’t understand; you’ll look, but you won’t see.

These people’s hearts have become hard. They barely hear, and they’ve shut their eyes. Otherwise, they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand in their hearts, turn back to me, and be healed.’
“But blessed are your eyes, because they see, and your ears, because they hear.
I’m telling you the truth: many prophets and righteous people longed to see what you see but didn’t, and to hear what you hear but didn’t.
“So listen to what the farmer’s parable means.
When someone hears the message about the Kingdom but doesn’t understand it, the evil one comes and snatches away what was planted in their heart. That’s the seed sown along the path.
The seed sown on rocky ground is someone who hears the message and immediately receives it with joy.
But they have no roots and last only a little while. When trouble or persecution comes because of the message, they quickly fall away.
The seed sown among thorns is someone who hears the message, but the worries of this age and the false promise of wealth choke it, so it produces nothing.
The seed sown on good soil is someone who hears and understands the message. They really do produce a crop—some a hundred times what was sown, some sixty, and some thirty.”
He told them another parable: “The Kingdom of Heaven is like a man who planted good seed in his field.
While everyone was asleep, his enemy came and planted darnel weeds among the wheat, then left.
When the wheat sprouted and produced grain, the weeds appeared too.
The landowner’s servants came and asked, ‘Sir, didn’t you plant good seed in your field? Where did these weeds come from?’
He told them, ‘An enemy did this.’ The servants asked, ‘Do you want us to go and pull the weeds out?’
‘No,’ he replied. ‘You might pull up the wheat along with the weeds.
Let them grow together until harvest. At harvest time I’ll tell the workers: “First gather the weeds and tie them in bundles to burn. Then gather the wheat into my barn.”’”
He told them another parable: “The Kingdom of Heaven is like a mustard seed that a man took and planted in his field.
It’s smaller than all the other seeds, but when it grows, it’s bigger than the garden plants and becomes a tree. The birds of the sky come and nest in its branches.”
He told them another parable: “The Kingdom of Heaven is like yeast that a woman mixed into three measures of flour until it was all leavened.”
Jesus taught the crowds all these things in parables. He didn’t speak to them without using a parable.
This fulfilled what the prophet had said: “I’ll speak in parables; I’ll reveal things hidden since the world began.”
Then Jesus sent the crowds away and went into a house. His disciples came to him and said, “Explain the parable about the weeds in the field.”
He answered, “The one who plants the good seed is the Son of Man.
The field is the world, and the good seed represents the people of the Kingdom. The weeds represent the people of the evil one.
The enemy who planted them is the devil. The harvest is the end of the age, and the workers are angels.
Just as the weeds are gathered up and burned, that’s what will happen at the end of this age.
The Son of Man will send his angels, and they’ll gather out of his Kingdom everything that causes people to sin and everyone who does evil.
They’ll throw them into the fiery furnace, where there will be weeping and grinding of teeth.
Then the righteous will shine like the sun in their Father’s Kingdom. Anyone with ears should listen.
“The Kingdom of Heaven is like treasure hidden in a field. A man found it and hid it again. Overjoyed, he sold everything he owned and bought that field.
“The Kingdom of Heaven is also like a merchant looking for fine pearls.
When he found one pearl of great value, he went and sold everything he owned and bought it.
“The Kingdom of Heaven is also like a net thrown into the sea that caught fish of every kind.
When it was full, the fishermen pulled it onto the shore. They sat down and put the good fish into containers, but threw the bad ones away.
That’s how it will be at the end of the age. The angels will come and separate the wicked from the righteous.
They’ll throw the wicked into the fiery furnace, where there will be weeping and grinding of teeth.”
“Have you understood all this?” Jesus asked. They answered, “Yes, Lord.”
He told them, “So every scribe who has become a disciple of the Kingdom of Heaven is like a homeowner who brings new and old things out of their treasure.”
When Jesus had finished these parables, he left there.
He returned to his hometown and taught in their synagogue. The people were amazed and said, “Where did he get this wisdom and these miracles?
Isn’t he the carpenter’s son? Isn’t his mother called Mary, and aren’t his brothers James, Joses, Simon, and Judas?
And aren’t all his sisters here with us? So where did he get all this?”
They took offense at him. But Jesus told them, “A prophet is honored everywhere except in his hometown and his own house.”
He didn’t do many miracles there because they didn’t believe.
